title: Can fine qualities become a drink?
odia:
ଗୁଣ ସୁନ୍ଦର ବୋଲି ଗୋଳି ପିଇବ କି
ରୂପ ସୁନ୍ଦର ବୋଲି ପାରି ଶୋଇବ କି?
literal_meaning: Because its qualities are fine, will you mix it up and drink it? Because its appearance is beautiful, will you spread it out and sleep on it?
meaning_odia: ଗୁଣ ଭଲ ବୋଲି କଣ ତାକୁ ଗୋଳି ପିଇହେବ, ରୂପ ସୁନ୍ଦର ବୋଲି କଣ ତାକୁ ବିଛାଇ ଶୋଇହେବ—ଏହି ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କଥାଟିର ଆଧାର। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଗୁଣ ବା ରୂପର ପ୍ରଶଂସା ମାତ୍ରରେ ସବୁ ବ୍ୟବହାରିକ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ପୂରଣ ହୁଏ ନାହିଁ; କେଉଁ କାମରେ କଣ ଲାଗିବ, ତାହା ମଧ୍ୟ ବିଚାର କରିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।
explanation: The two questions turn praise into deliberately awkward practical tests: can admired qualities be mixed into a drink, or beauty spread out to sleep on? Our editorial reading distinguishes admiration from usefulness for a particular need. The verse leaves its target unnamed, so the comparison can remain broad.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A group admires an object’s finish but finds it unsuitable for the job they need done. A reader recalls the verse’s questions to distinguish what is attractive from what serves the purpose.
cultural_context: The repeated ସୁନ୍ଦର ବୋଲି introduces a reason that each question then tests. Drinking and sleeping are concrete actions placed against abstract qualities and appearance. Their mismatch gives the questions their sceptical force.

english_summary: Admiration alone does not establish usefulness for a particular need.
